title: kb_mcp.py --status does not say when the project's registered kb server runs another clone
goal: kb_mcp.py --status (and /kb-setup's MCP step, which reads it) reads the kb server registered for this project (local, then project scope) and, when its kb_mcp.py lies in another clone, prints that clone's path, its commit and how far behind it is, with the command that re-registers this clone (kb_mcp.py --register-local), so a session never answers from another clone unawares. Found in SP-eahtellz on the Windows host: the local registration ran C:/Users/Public/it-ops-kb-perf (3,404 commits behind), whose kb_pack lacked the Defender facts committed that day. The repro is host-bound: it reads this host's registration, which names it-ops-kb-perf until it is re-registered.

run: import subprocess,sys;r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kb_mcp.py','--status'],capture_output=True,text=True);o=r.stdout+r.stderr;bad='it-ops-kb-perf' not in o;print('status names the registered server clone:',not bad);sys.exit(r.returncode or int(bad))
